methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $5.7B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 1 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 2 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
The Boring Company, a Series G transportation venture that has raised $908M to date, is valued at $5.7B post-money on its most recent financing. The Transportation sector comp universe is limited; two private peers (Rivian and Einride) are identifiable, though neither provides sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable data to support a reliable peer-median valuation method.

Given data constraints, stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable triangulation method. Applying a standard 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement to the $5.7B base valuation yields $7.1B. This mechanic assumes normalized stage-to-stage appreciation holds despite the company's founder status and sector positioning.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6.1B (low) to $8.2B (high), with a median of $7.1B. Material uncertainties include the absence of narrow-peer benchmarking, which limits anchoring to comparable growth trajectories and exit multiples in Transportation infrastructure. The single-method foundation also leaves the estimate sensitive to assumptions about stage progression velocity. Further resolution would require either a deeper private comp set in adjacent stages or visibility into market comparables for deployed tunnel and boring assets.
